reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

title.narrative: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices Annual Report: October 2023 - Sept 2024

description.narrative: The program facilitated the establishment of safe and institutionalized spaces for dialogue between youth, government institutions, and political actors through the creation of the Office of the Citizen, which worked closely with county-based youth organizations like County Rights & Voice CBO to facilitate consistent communication and improve local governance. Additionally, supported youth-led advocacy initiatives that addressed key governance issues, such as waste management in Oyugis town (Homa Bay County) , the completion of public health facilities like the Osiepe dispensary, and infrastructure concerns like the lack of toilets at Awuoro Primary School. These advocacy efforts led to tangible improvements in public services and increased accountability from local authorities. Youth civic champions in counties such as Nairobi, Kericho, and Lamu identified and addressed local governance challenges, including waste disposal, public safety, and access to National IDs, by engaging local authorities and driving change. Their efforts included reviving stalled projects, such as the Youth Bill in Kericho, and advocating for better waste management and public infrastructure in Busia. The program also built the capacity of youth to hold local governments accountable, with youth-led committees in Nairobi, Lamu, and Kericho successfully addressing issues such as substandard school toilets and environmental hazards like untreated sewage. Collaboration with local community-based organizations (CBOs) like the Lamu Art and Theatre Alliance further strengthened the program’s impact, enabling youth to raise issues such as delayed National ID issuance and the sale of alcohol to minors. These partnerships enhanced youth advocacy efforts and raised awareness on critical local governance issues. Regional youth forums were organized across counties such as Homabay, Busia, and Mombasa, providing a platform for youth to share concerns, build advocacy strategies, and foster stronger links between youth, government, and the community. Youth leaders in Kericho and Busia mobilized their communities to address governance challenges, demonstrating a deeper commitment to democratic processes. The program saw a marked increase in youth engagement, with more youth leaders taking on the role of civic actors, advocating for change, and voicing concerns about issues such as water shortages, healthcare challenges, land grabbing, and unsafe infrastructure. Their ability to draft advocacy letters and engage local authorities signified their growing influence in governance. Moreover, local youth organizations like the Isangalo Art Group in Busia demonstrated increased advocacy capacity by addressing issues like healthcare service delivery and influencing local governance. Expanded dialogue platforms like town hall meetings, sports dialogues, and art expos facilitated deeper engagement with community members and local government officials. These initiatives provided youth with the tools to influence decision-making processes and allowed them to effectively advocate for their communities' needs. As a result, these youth-led organizations gained legitimacy and strengthened their capacity to advocate for long-term governance improvements, ensuring that their voices remain a key part of the development process in their communities.
